title: Devin operating card correction status
summary: This intermediate-level resource determines whether the existing Devin operating card can be corrected safely. It provides a verification procedure for recovering the baseline, identifying the changed source, and limiting the correction to affected claims.
prerequisites: Access to the current committed devin-operating-card.json file and its revision history
Access to the catalogue schema and identifier registry
Network access for checking the cited first-party documentation

sections.title: Answer and source change
paragraphs: No. An intermediate practitioner should not rely on or replace the existing operating card until its committed contents and supporting first-party documentation have been recovered.

The cited source that requires correction is content/resources/coding-tools/devin-operating-card.json. It is an unregistered local path and was never verified. Whether the original source moved or merely exceeded its review cadence is UNKNOWN because the old source record, former URL, verification date, and source contents are unavailable.

The claims affected by the source change are UNKNOWN because the existing procedures and their citation relationships are unavailable. Devin-specific interface names, workflows, controls, expected outputs, failure states, versions, and configuration keys are therefore omitted rather than asserted. Material unaffected by the change is also UNKNOWN, so no claim can be designated safe to edit or preserve without the baseline.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: First, obtain the exact committed contents and revision history of devin-operating-card.json. If the file or its history cannot be obtained, stop the correction and request the baseline from the repository owner rather than reconstructing it from the title.

Second, retrieve every source recorded in the baseline and identify the former and replacement HTTPS locations. If a source does not resolve, do not substitute an unofficial page; request a current first-party location and keep the affected claims marked UNKNOWN until it can be checked.

Third, compare the old source with the current first-party source and map each changed passage to the precise card claims it supported. If a claim has no current first-party support, omit that claim from the corrected procedures and record it as UNKNOWN in the review notes.

Fourth, modify only the source record and the claims shown by the comparison to be affected. If the baseline cannot be compared exactly, do not commit a replacement because preserving unaffected material cannot be demonstrated.

Finally, validate the corrected object against the platform Resource schema and check its identifier against the complete catalogue. If schema validation or the uniqueness check fails, correct the reported conflict and repeat both checks before publication.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence consists of the recovered baseline and revision, the old source record, a successfully retrieved first-party replacement URL, the date of that retrieval, a claim-by-claim change record, a minimal diff, successful schema validation, and confirmation that devin-operating-card is unique across the catalogue.

Verify the correction by confirming that each retained Devin-specific claim is supported by the retrieved first-party source, every changed claim appears in the change record, and the diff contains no unrelated edits. Also confirm that every failure-capable procedure has a stated next action and that the final JSON parses as one object.

That evidence is not available in the supplied material. Verification status is therefore UNKNOWN, and the next action is to recover the baseline, schema, catalogue registry, and current first-party documentation before publishing an operational correction.
